Subject: Analytics vendor triage and consolidation plan

Team —

We have three analytics renewals coming up across product and API telemetry: Amplitude (product tracking, renewal 2027-06-30), Segment (server-side API event routing, renewal 2027-07-15), and a small Mixpanel contract used by Email Experiments (renewal 2027-08-01). Finance asked us to evaluate consolidation scenarios that reduce unit cost and simplify billing while preserving current integrations.

Attached: renewal_summary_q2.pdf (high-level spend & usage).

Ask: please review the attachment and reply with 2 things by EOD Friday: 1) one recommended path (keep as-is / consolidate to Amplitude / consolidate to Segment / hybrid + phased migration), and 2) any hard constraints (data residency, SSA, Feature parity blockers).

Notes: Product prefers Amplitude for event-level analysis; API/platform prefers Segment for routing flexibility. Procurement (Karthik) — we’ll need your input on timing and minimal lead times for contract consolidation.

Thanks —
Rishi

Thanks, Rishi — quick procurement perspective:

- Timing: Contract renewals are staggered, so we have a ~6–10 week runway to negotiate terms before we must execute (Segment is the near term).
- Constraints: Billing/legal needs a single SOW per vendor; any consolidation requires a new SOW and 30-day countersign window.
- Acceptance criteria: Pricing per MAU / event, guaranteed data export (S3), SOC2 + ISO attestation, KMS integration for event exports.

Summary from product side after quick run of usage:

- Amplitude: primary for product funnel analysis & cohorts. We rely on user-level retention sessions and raw event exports for ML experiments. Feature-wise it’s closest to what PMs use today.
- Segment: we use it for API-side event routing (third-party sinks, transformations) — switching away would require building routing or using a replacement that supports server-side transformations.
- Mixpanel: minimal usage (email experiments). Could be sunseted if we migrate the small workload to Amplitude events.

Recommendation (short): Hybrid-first: Keep Segment for routing + consolidate product analytics into Amplitude. Phase 1: Move Mixpanel workloads into Amplitude (low risk). Phase 2: Evaluate replacing Segment routing with a smaller message bus + lightweight transformer if cost savings justify dev work.

Hard blockers: Need guaranteed raw export to S3 (daily) and event-level TTL controls for compliance.

Marissa
Senior Product Manager — Observability
